interface_name.description: Name of the virtual TAP interface (e.g., n2n0, tap0).

mac_address.description: MAC address for the virtual interface; use 'auto' to generate a random one.

ip_address.description: Static IPv4 address and CIDR netmask for the interface (e.g., 10.42.10.2/24).

supernodes.description: List of supernode addresses to bootstrap the mesh. At least one is required.

community.description: Shared community name (case-sensitive). All edges must use the same community to join the mesh.

encryption.description: Cipher algorithm for payload encryption. Supported: 'none', 'aes', 'twofish', 'blowfish', 'cast5'.

encryption_key.description: Encryption key (base64-encoded or plain). Required if encryption ≠ 'none'. Leave blank for 'none'.

listen_port.description: Local UDP port to listen on for incoming P2P connections. Use 0 to let the OS choose.

enable_multicast.description: Enable multicast peer discovery to locate peers locally (requires multicast support).

ttl.description: IP TTL for forwarded packets. Lower values limit hop count (e.g., 1 = local network only).

pid_file.description: Path to write the process PID file.

log_file.description: Path to write log output. Empty string disables file logging.

log_level.description: Verbosity of logging: 0 (quiet) to 4 (debug). 2 (warn) is recommended for production.

keepalive_interval.description: Seconds between keepalive packets (0 to disable). Helps maintain NAT traversal.

max_edges.description: Maximum peers allowed in this community (0 = unlimited). Helps prevent resource exhaustion.

drop_privileges.description: User:group to drop to after startup for security (e.g., n2n:nobody).

direct_connection.description: Attempt direct peer-to-peer connection (bypass supernode) when possible (improves latency).

state_file.description: Optional persistent state file for edge registration (used by some supernodes).

only_registered_edges.description: Reject connections from peers not registered with this edge (requires external auth).

extra_opts.description: Extra command-line arguments (e.g., '--daemon --pid-file /run/n2n/n2n.pid'). Use with caution.
